subsystems.name: EMG electrode array
subsystems.role: detects electrical signals from the small muscles that control finger movement.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplifies and filters the tiny muscle signals.

subsystems.name: Embedded processor
subsystems.role: runs machine-learning models to classify gestures in real time.

subsystems.name: Wireless radio
subsystems.role: sends commands to phones, computers or headsets.

subsystems.name: Power and housing
subsystems.role: provides energy and keeps electrodes in stable contact with the skin.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode layout
buildSteps.detail: Simulate and test where on the finger or hand to place electrodes to best capture signals from the small muscles that move fingers.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the flexible circuit
buildSteps.detail: Print conductive traces and mount electrodes on a flexible printed circuit board that can bend around the finger.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: Attach the analog front end, processor, radio and battery to the flexible circuit.

buildSteps.title: Collect training data
buildSteps.detail: Record EMG signals from many people performing a set of finger micro-gestures, such as tapping or pinching.

buildSteps.title: Train the machine-learning model
buildSteps.detail: Use the data to train a classifier that maps signal patterns to specific commands, optimizing for low power.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the ring
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the electronics in a biocompatible shell, ensuring electrodes protrude slightly to contact the skin.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate per user
buildSteps.detail: A short guided session adapts the model to the individual's unique muscle signals.

buildSteps.title: Validate performance
buildSteps.detail: Test gesture recognition accuracy, battery life, comfort and wireless reliability across users.

prerequisites.why: Existing dry electrodes can pick up signals, but maintaining good contact on a moving finger without gel is still a challenge.
Modern microcontrollers and accelerators can run small neural networks within a milliwatt budget.
Provides a standard, low-energy way to send commands to devices.
Lab systems can classify a handful of gestures, but generalizing across people and sessions remains difficult.
Small lithium-polymer cells fit inside a ring, though battery life is limited.

pathway.milestone: Wrist-worn EMG research prototypes (e.g., Meta's neural wristband) demonstrate gesture control.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that non-invasive muscle signals can drive simple digital actions.

pathway.milestone: Ring-form EMG devices with reliable finger micro-gesture detection.
pathway.unlocks: Discreet, always-available input for phones, AR glasses and computers.

pathway.milestone: Integration with productivity and accessibility software.
pathway.unlocks: Hands-free control for people with motor impairments and seamless multitasking.

pathway.milestone: Decoding intended actions without visible movement.
pathway.unlocks: A true neural interface that feels like reading thoughts, though this remains speculative.
